source_caption:
American Pie is a classic teen comedy that follows four high school friends—Jim, Kevin, Oz, and Finch—who make a pact to lose their virginity before graduation. The film mixes awkward situations, sexual curiosity, and friendship struggles as each character tries different approaches to relationships and confidence. Jim, played by Jason Biggs, becomes the most memorable character due to his embarrassing and hilarious misadventures, including the iconic pie scene.

The movie became popular for its bold humor and honest (though exaggerated) portrayal of teenage life, setting the tone for many teen comedies that followed. Directed by Paul Weitz, it balances crude jokes with moments about friendship and growing up. Over time, American Pie turned into a successful franchise, influencing pop culture and launching the careers of several actors while becoming a defining film of late 90s teen comedy.

source_details.synopsis: American Pie is a 1999 American teen comedy film directed and co-produced by Paul Weitz and written by Adam Herz. The film's main ensemble cast includes Jason Biggs, Chris Klein, Alyson Hannigan, Natasha Lyonne, Thomas Ian Nicholas, Tara Reid, Mena Suvari, Eddie Kaye Thomas, and Seann William Scott, with Eugene Levy, Shannon Elizabeth, Chris Owen, and Jennifer Coolidge in supporting roles. The coming-of-age story follows a group of high school classmates who make a pact to lose their virginity before they graduate. After the success of Wes Craven's horror teen film Scream (1996), Herz began developing the script for American Pie, originally titled Untitled Teenage Sex Comedy That Can Be Made
